summary: Camizestrant (Etcamah) is a next-generation oral selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) and complete estrogen receptor antagonist granted accelerated approval September 4, 2026, in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib, palbociclib, or ribociclib) for adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer upon detection of an ESR1 mutation during aromatase inhibitor and CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy. Approval was based on the Phase 3 SERENA-6 trial, which showed a 56 percent reduction in risk of progression or death. The recommended dose is 75 mg orally once daily, with or without food, plus the CDK4/6 inhibitor until progression or unacceptable toxicity. It carries a BOXED WARNING for increased risk of arrhythmias when combined with ribociclib or other QTc-prolonging drugs, plus warnings for bradycardia and embryo-fetal toxicity. Common adverse effects include neutropenia, photopsia, infections, diarrhea, nausea, anemia, fatigue, and bradycardia.
indications: Treatment of adults with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer upon detection of an estrogen receptor-1 (ESR1) mutation during aromatase inhibitor and CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy, in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (accelerated approval September 4, 2026, based on SERENA-6)

moa: Camizestrant (Etcamah) is a next-generation oral selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) and complete estrogen receptor antagonist. It binds the estrogen receptor, blocks its transcriptional activity, and induces receptor degradation, depriving HR-positive breast cancer cells of estrogen-driven growth signaling. It retains activity against tumors bearing ESR1 mutations that emerge under prior endocrine therapy and cause resistance to aromatase inhibitors.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to camizestrant or any excipient
Concomitant ribociclib or other QTc-prolonging drugs where the combination poses unacceptable arrhythmia risk (see boxed warning) - avoid the combination
monitor: ECG (QTc) and electrolytes, especially with any QTc-prolonging medicine
Heart rate and symptoms of bradycardia (dizziness, syncope, fatigue)
Visual symptoms (flashes of light, blurred vision)
Complete blood counts per the CDK4/6 inhibitor labeling
relative: Pre-existing bradycardia, conduction disease, or low resting heart rate
Congenital long QT, electrolyte abnormalities, or other arrhythmia risk factors
Concomitant medicines that slow heart rate

preg: Based on its mechanism of action and animal findings, camizestrant can cause fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and after the last dose per prescribing information.
lact: There are no data on the presence of camizestrant in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and after the final dose per prescribing information.
renal: No established dose adjustment in renal impairment. Monitor closely in moderate to severe impairment and follow the co-administered CDK4/6 inhibitor labeling.
hepatic: No established dose adjustment; monitor in hepatic impairment and follow the co-administered CDK4/6 inhibitor labeling for its hepatic guidance.

interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol due to additive fatigue and gastrointestinal effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor ECG (QTc), heart rate, electrolytes, and pregnancy status; monitor blood counts per the CDK4/6 inhibitor labeling.
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; swallow tablets whole.
major: Ribociclib and other QTc-prolonging drugs - BOXED WARNING for increased arrhythmia risk in combination; avoid the combination
Drugs that cause bradycardia (beta blockers, certain calcium channel blockers, digoxin, antiarrhythmics) - additive heart rate lowering; avoid or monitor closely
minor: No major CYP-mediated interaction requiring dose change is established in the summary labeling; review concomitant medicines per full prescribing information.
moderate: Other agents that lower heart rate or blood pressure - additive bradycardia and hypotension; monitor

common: Neutropenia and leukopenia (with CDK4/6 inhibitor combination)
Visual effects including photopsia (flashes of light)
emergency: Syncope, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat (possible arrhythmia, boxed warning) - seek emergency care
Severe dizziness or fainting with very slow pulse (bradycardia)
Fever with very low white cell counts (possible neutropenic infection)
rare: Severe QTc prolongation with torsades de pointes (with QTc-prolonging combinations)
serious: QTc interval prolongation with increased arrhythmia risk when combined with ribociclib or other QTc-prolonging drugs (BOXED WARNING)
Visual disturbances interfering with daily activities

monitoring: ECG for QTc prolongation, especially with ribociclib or other QTc-prolonging drugs (boxed warning)
Heart rate and symptoms of bradycardia at baseline and periodically

Blood counts and other monitoring per the co-administered CDK4/6 inhibitor labeling
counsel: Take 75 mg once daily, with or without food, plus your CDK4/6 inhibitor exactly as prescribed

BOXED WARNING: when combined with ribociclib or other drugs that prolong the QTc interval, there is an increased risk of serious heart rhythm problems - report palpitations, fainting, or severe dizziness at once
Report slow pulse, dizziness, fainting, or unusual fatigue (possible bradycardia)
Tell your team about flashes of light or other vision changes
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed; tell your doctor about all heart, blood pressure, and rhythm medicines

Per prescribing information; dosed once daily
Continuous ER suppression with daily dosing until progression or unacceptable toxicity

pearls: Next-generation SERD and complete ER antagonist active against emergent ESR1 mutations; paired with Guardant360 CDx companion diagnostic
SERENA-6 showed a 56 percent reduction in risk of progression or death for the combination
BOXED WARNING: increased arrhythmia risk with ribociclib or other QTc-prolonging drugs - avoid those combinations
Dose- and baseline-dependent heart rate lowering: avoid concomitant bradycardia drugs and monitor pulse
Photopsia (flashes of light) is characteristic and dose-related; counsel patients it is usually low grade
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day, then resume the regular schedule. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for camizestrant overdose. Manage with supportive care including cardiac monitoring (heart rate and ECG for bradycardia and QTc changes) and correction of electrolyte abnormalities. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
